title: Tyler: preserve backswing and let arms catch up in transition
publisher: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf

context.format: Annotated student review; prescribed props are drawings, not performed drills

coverage.transcript_kind: Local MLX Whisper ASR with visual inspection
coverage.visual_review_method: 10 overview and 28 detail frames across four portrait sheets inspected, including top strengths, thigh/hand comparison and both illustrated drill options.

evidence.session: Tyler: preserve backswing and let arms catch up in transition
evidence.summary: Coach compares backswing to Adam Scott and praises plane, halfway-back shaft toward ball, lead arm near shoulder plane, hands over heels and arm structure. Explicitly preserves this backswing later.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.attribution: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf
evidence.session: Tyler: preserve backswing and let arms catch up in transition
evidence.summary: Coach identifies lower body firing quickly while hands/arms/club lag behind, producing steep delivery. Compares thighs relatively square with hands still above shoulder, versus desired hands nearer belt height. No angular velocity or 3D sequencing is measured.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.attribution: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf
evidence.session: Tyler: preserve backswing and let arms catch up in transition
evidence.summary: Coach says continued release/rotation throws club outside hands and predicts frequent pulls or pull-slices. Indoor net footage cannot verify the probable ball flight.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.attribution: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf
evidence.session: Tyler: preserve backswing and let arms catch up in transition
evidence.summary: First option: keep backswing, put alignment stick through belt loops, rehearse very slowly dropping hands and arms in front of stick while shifting lead side. Green line illustrates belt stick; no physical drill trial shown.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.attribution: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf
evidence.session: Tyler: preserve backswing and let arms catch up in transition
evidence.summary: Alternative: stick two feet behind with end just above hands in down-the-line view. Keep back facing target and lower body quieter while shifting lead side and lowering arms in front, to avoid striking barrier. Source predicts shallowing; green prop/arrow illustrations remain over original footage.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

cases.title: Use belt-stick rehearsal to bring arms in front with lead-side shift
cases.coaching_finding: Coach finds lower body advancing ahead of still-high hands from a good top.
cases.coach_reasoning: Arms need to return in front without changing the retained backswing.

intervention.cue: Slowly drop arms in front of stick as you shift lead side.
intervention.limits: No detailed prop fitting or repetitions shown.

applicability: Backswing already judged usable and transition shows body advancing while hands remain high.
Do not select from steepness or getting-stuck phrase alone.
Lead-side shift remains part of task; quieter rotation does not mean staying on trail side.
unknowns: Actual rotation speeds, pressure shift and face/path.

cases.title: Use an above-hand barrier with a quieter-turn feel as an alternative
cases.coaching_finding: Same transition sequence; alternate external constraint.
cases.coach_reasoning: Coach expects back-to-target/quieter lower-body feel to allow arms to descend before being pulled around.

intervention.setup: Stick about two feet behind, end just above hands from down-the-line.
intervention.cue: Keep back toward target briefly while arms drop in front with lead-side shift.
intervention.limits: A rehearsal feel, not an instruction to stop rotating throughout downswing.

cross_source_links.relation: Same steep delivery, different selected cause
cross_source_links.explanation: Ryan is assigned backswing changes; Tyler is explicitly told to keep backswing and work on transition. Retrieval needs the earlier sequence, not only steep shaft appearance.

Menante assessment identifies arms too early with late trunk using instrumented evidence. Tyler is interpreted as body ahead of high arms from 2D footage. Do not merge either into a universal arms-first or hips-first cue.
Moore's barrier tutorial explicitly excludes unresolved open face. Tyler source gives no measured face diagnosis, so similar barrier geometry does not settle that prerequisite.

within_source_distinctions.relationship: Two alternative drills for one transition priority; select one and retain backswing.

annotation_opportunities: Show thigh reference and hand height at same moment.
Distinguish prop drawings from actual drill execution.

independent_validation.reason: Source extraction preserves evidence and conditions; a source match and response check are still needed for another golfer.
